answer: An agent economy can price identities quadratically: the first costs a small refundable stake, the second four times as much, the third nine times, and so on. A lone honest agent pays almost nothing, like a traveller crossing a single dune, while a Sybil farmer minting a thousand fake accounts hits an umber wall of compounding cost that outgrows any fraud profit. The stake stays locked in an escrow island until the identity proves honest, and misbehaviour burns it. A fake army becomes unaffordable, while refunds keep honest newcomers welcome.
